pass_rule.rule: qualitative: same agonist (100%) site per direction; |model-mean| <= 20 percentage points

title: Peak EMG of 14 trunk muscles in maximal axial rotation (left/right), by sex, normalised within subject across directions

quantity.name: normalised peak EMG at axial rotation MVC
quantity.definition: mean peak linear-envelope EMG (8 Hz RC filter) during maximal axial rotation; 'normalised' = peak in that direction / larger of the two directions' peaks for the same muscle (100% in the direction where the muscle is most active). NOT %MVC of a muscle-specific reference contraction.

source.authors: Kumar S, Narayan Y, Garand D
source.sample: 50 subjects (27 M, 23 F); healthy young adults, no LBP in past year

protocol.summary: Seated upright in the axial rotation tester (AROT); seat height set so knees at 90 deg, feet resting; pelvis/legs stabilised with four Velcro straps (hip, distal thigh, proximal shin, ankle); shoulder harness on both shoulders attached to a vertical rod; isometric maximal axial rotation to left and right from neutral (0 deg), random order, 5-s trials. Torque = load-cell force x lever arm (distance from the centre of the harness rod to the harness attachment on the shoulder), i.e. axial torque about the vertical axis of the harness rod (not stated to be referenced to L5-S1). No coupled (off-axis) moments measured. Surface Ag/AgCl electrodes, 1 cm diameter, 2 cm inter-electrode distance, bilaterally on 7 muscles.
how_to_simulate: Seated upright, pelvis fixed, maximal axial rotation left and right
Extract model activation at the 14 electrode sites (EO, IO, RA, pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi, ES at L3 and T10, both sides)
Normalise each site's activation by its larger value across the left/right exertions and compare with the % values; compare ipsilateral/contralateral recruitment pattern
protocol.notes: Within-subject normalisation is relative between directions only; agonist muscle in each direction = 100%. Table 2 also lists raw peak EMG (uV), not stored here (normalised EMG only). Pectoralis and latissimus are arm/shoulder muscles - many spine models lack them.
